newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir completes docking despite last-minute problems.
newsitem.headline: Mir completes docking despite last-minute problems.

text.p: A Progress supply craft redocked with Russia's Mir space station on Monday but only after Mir's commander took manual control of Progress at the last minute when the automatic pilot failed, officials said.

"At a distance of 260 metres (yards) there was a hitch on the on-board system and therefore the command to go to manual pilot was given," Yuri Semyonov, general director of the Energia rocket corporation, told reporters. "The crew did a great job in doing the manual docking."
Other problems also appeared to have developed on Mir in the wake of the docking.
"The Mir station has somewhat lost its orientation toward the Sun and there has appeared a deficit of energy," Semyonov said.
He did not immediately provide details of how much power had been lost or how easy it would be to correct this latest problem.

The redocking manoeuvre repeated a procedure carried out on June 25, when a different Progress vehicle docking with Mir collided with the station's Spektr module, causing a major loss of power in the worst accident in Mir's 11-year history.
Several areas of the station have been out of action since then because the station lacks sufficient power.

Mission Control officials said the automatic pilot failed 13 minutes before the docking, forcing Mir's commander Anatoly Solovyov, one of Rusia's most experienced cosmonauts, to take control of the docking. The docking was completed at 1653 (1253 GMT).
It was not immediately clear why the automatic pilot failed, but it was the latest in a series of technical glitches that have plagued the space station in recent months.
On Sunday, an earlier attempt to redock Progress was cancelled because of a computer programming error.
After Monday's redocking the atmosphere appeared tense at Mission Control outside Moscow, with groups of officials discussing the situation near the computers and monitors of the operations centre.

Progress delivered oxygen, food, water and tools to Mir on July 7 and is now filled mostly with garbage. Redocking a rubbish-filled module will provide better balance for Mir and will protect its hatch from prolonged solar exposure.
Progress undocked on August 6 to make room for a Soyuz spaceship bringing Solovyov and his flight engineer from Earth.
